body: This seems unnecessary. You clear all of p_buffer up above, and nothing has changed anything in buf before now, so it should already be clear.
Huh? This is c, nothing is cleared if we don't manually clear it.
Good catch! This must have been before I added to pre-clear code. I've removed the extra zeroing out.

When `stop()` on the next line is propagated to `base_playback`, even if it would try to handle stopping gracefully with a short fade out to avoid a click, that fade out would be truncated here, and on the consequent mix calls if the fade out crosses the mix buffer boundary, since `active` of would be `false` at this outer layer.

If that's intended, or if the idea is that the user can do the math to find out that at `scheduled_end_frame` the source is going to be at a safe silent point to stop rendering, maybe this should be documented.

However, this still works if the user knows to avoid the click and/or makes sure to fade out beforehand.
